update_engine: Support milestones to EOL from Omaha Initiative to show EOL message on Chrome OS devices require that update_engine parses the fields within Omaha response that pertain to the new milestones to EOL field. The Omaha response will include a new field called "milestones_to_eol" which will be an integer value string. The job of update_engine when it comes to milestones to EOL from Omaha is to merely forward. No checks and no modifications of fields are done within update_engine besides being able to convert the milestones to EOL from a string to integer. shill: routing_table: Provide support for 32-bit routing table IDs The Linux kernel moved from 8-bit to 32-bit routing table IDs in v2.6. However, the historical 8-bit size of routing table IDs is ossified in the rtmsg structure [0]. To get around this, the RTA_TABLE and FRA_TABLE attributes were introduced to carry 32-bit IDs. When the table ID cannot fit in a byte, the rtmsg table ID field is instead set to RT_TABLE_COMPAT. This change updates Shill's routing system to support 32-bit routing table IDs. This will come in handy when providing support for using the accept_ra_rt_table sysctl. [0] https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.0/source/include/uapi/linux/rtnetlink.h#L206 BUG=chromium:941597 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Manual testing with adding 1000 to all allocated table IDs. Change-Id: Iec189aefbfb00484baa286601f18298755b0ea42 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1758536 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

Refactor Tast tests for Assistant. This change: 1. Splits the original assistant_text_queries.go into two separate test files: assistant_time_query.go and assistant_volume_queries.go, because they no more share the same deps list (volume tests need "audio_play" dep while time query doesn't). Also this makes it possible for us to push them to CQ later separately if one is stablized faster than the other. 2. Adds extra logic in assistant_time_query.go to handle different time notations (e.g. 12-hout/24-hour clock convert, different languages). 3. Adds assistant_simple_queries.go which contains a simple math query test. We were trying to test the basic functionality of Assistant (answering a simple query correctly) by sending a time query before. But we observed there are still some uncertainty for the time response, e.g. languages, time notations, etc. So we try to use a simple math query instead since it probably has a more uniform answer regardless of different time zone or language. BUG=None. TEST=run all affected tests locally. diagnostics: update cros_healthd's init script cros_healthd's ProbeNonRemovableBlockDevices method works outside of the minijail sandbox, but not inside. To fix this, we need to mount parts of /sys and /dev inside the minijail. cros_healthd attempts to discover nonremovable block devices programmatically, so it doesn't make sense to mount specific paths within /sys or /dev when these paths could vary per device or over time. Also, add the -G argument to the minijail call, so that cros_healthd enters the minijail as a member of the disk group. This is necessary to get access to the block /dev nodes. BUG=b:128683357 TEST=build and deploy diagnostics on nami. Add some test code to DeviceStatusCollector in Chrome which calls cros_healthd's ProbeNonRemovableBlockDevices Mojo method. Enterprise enroll the DUT, then check /var/log/chrome/chrome to make sure that Chrome was able to read information from cros_healthd. Change-Id: Ia157eaed0313058527e5afc9dddcac56a6f0f61c Signed-off-by: Paul Moy <pmoy@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1752326 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>
